Only B (green, colour-split, dashed box about [294,182,532,448]) is drawn. The raw frame shows the white-gi athlete being thrown by the blue-gi athlete. Their white jacket hem and black belt are visible around x 400-520, y 240-330, and their white trousers run down to a bare foot at about (530,480). The head and upper torso are partly hidden behind the blue athlete, but the lower torso and both legs are plainly visible. tracks.json frame 136 has A status "lost", box null, note "occluded in merged box". The neighbouring frames 135 and 137 both give A a colour_split box (about [401,188,536,458] and [392,182,548,420]), so the visible body was trackable and the loss is a one-frame dropout. The claim holds as written: A has no box or skeleton while the body is visible. Severity high is plausible.

Frame alignment: I read the raw and annotated videos sequentially and checked pixel difference. Raw 142 matches annotated 142 (mean abs diff 4.2, versus 14 or more for neighbouring frames). The first seek-based raw extraction was off by several frames, so I discarded it.

Raw frame 142: the white-gi athlete is clearly visible mid-throw, though motion-blurred. The dark head is at roughly x=580, y=330. White gi legs and torso are at roughly x=420-560, y=300-490, with a bare foot near (545, 470). All of this is on screen and not hidden behind the blue athlete, so a visible athlete has no A overlay.

Temporal check: annotated 139 also reads "A: LOST (no pose)" with no red overlay, while the white athlete is visible in the throw. At 139 the green skeleton and box for B also cover part of the white-gi body, so the mismatch is not a one-frame glitch. Annotated 145 shows A "detected 0.20", with a red box and skeleton on the white athlete's legs. A is therefore lost across about frames 139-142 and is recovered by 145.

Conclusion: the claim holds exactly at frame 142. A is LOST with no overlay while the white athlete's head and legs are clearly visible. I found nothing that refutes it.
